title: Override hook invocation in Hunch's own checkout to use in-tree build
context: When Hunch installs its own hooks during development, the invocation string is baked in at install time from the installing process's build (which may be a different version or location). Later, when hooks fire and regenerate committed docs (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md), they call the installer's build, not the repo's own generator, causing silent drift that only test/grounding-freshness.test.ts catches. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Detect when hooks are installed inside Hunch's own source tree (by checking if package.json name matches HUNCH_PACKAGE_NAME) and force doc-regenerating invocations (post-commit sync, post-merge grounding-refresh) to always call back into that checkout's in-tree `npx tsx src/cli/index.ts`, overriding whatever invocation was passed at install time. Other projects depending on Hunch use the passed invocation unchanged.
consequences: Hunch's committed docs stay fresh across different global/npx installs within its own repo
The grounding-freshness test now passes reliably in dogfooding scenarios
Other projects depending on Hunch are unaffected — no behavior change for them
Only doc-regenerating operations are affected; repair-provenance keeps the passed invocation
Hook scripts remain per-machine and uncommitted (existing philosophy preserved)
alternatives_rejected: Accept silent drift in committed docs and disable the freshness test
Move detection and override logic to hook-execution time (requires changing hook scripts themselves)
Make invoking process responsible for handling version conflicts (can't solve install-time problem)
Disable hook doc regeneration entirely in Hunch's own checkout (loses the benefit of freshness verification)
